To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
social status seeking has a positive impact on growth only when savings is low or when productivity of capital is also low.
social status seeking may have a positive impact on growth, but only when saving is not too low and when the productivity of physical capital is not too high.
social status seeking can be a social incentive mechanism for wealth accumulation and growth when the productivity of the capital is low and when saving is low.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the impact of the social norm of status seeking on economic growth is positive only if the level of savings is low or if the productivity of capital in production is low.
status seeking is not a necessary condition for growth.
social status seeking can be seen as a norm of behaviour which is a source of wealth accumulation in the economy, but only when the saving propensity or the productivity of capital are low.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the impact of social status seeking on economic growth is positive when the productivity of the capital is low.
social status seeking may lead to economic growth only if the society is poor or if social status seeking is a strong incentive mechanism for savings.
the social status concern behaviour is a mixed blessing: it may have a negative or a positive effect on the rate of economic growth.
The main takeaway from our work is that
social status seeking may not be desirable for economic growth, especially when agents have high savings rates and high productivity of capital.
social status seeking can be a positive force for economic development, but only under some conditions.
the normative aspect of social status seeking is crucial for economic growth and that the norm is not always desirable.
